transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-04
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~63 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Lee (Redwood AE), Sanjay Patel (Redwood CSM), Elena Ruiz (Redwood SE), Ava Thompson (Pinehaven Head of ML), Derek Cho (Platform Eng), Nina Ruiz (Security Lead), Ravi Menon (Product), Sam (intern)

Summary:
Quick handoff from sales to activation, review of the activation playbook, runbook items for VPC/staging, SSO/KMS/security checklist, initial bench/soak plan for pilot, and explicit next steps to provision staging and schedule performance window. Some minor audio transcription errors present (names/terms garbled at times).

Topics covered:
- Activation playbook overview and timeline
- Networking: VPC, peering, CIDR, egress rules
- Authentication & secrets: SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM options
- Environment parity: staging data, sample payloads, KV cache behaviour
- Pilot success criteria: latency SLOs, cost targets, token budgets
- Operational handoff: runbook ownership and SLAs

Action items (pulled out for clarity): see metadata action_items list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Morgan Lee: Hey everyone, thank you for joining. I'm Morgan, I'll run point for the activation, with Sanjay and Elena from our side. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Ava Thompson: Doing good, thanks. Excited to get this moving.
[00:15] Derek Cho: Yep, ready. We just want to confirm we get a predictable runway to try dedicated vs hosted during the pilot.
[00:22] Morgan Lee: Totally, that's the goal. Today is less about sales and more about the actual handoff: the playbook, the staging network details, and the bench test. We'll confirm owners and dates.
[00:34] Sanjay Patel: Quick intro from me — CSM on the account, I'll run the onboarding sprints and post-launch adoption.
[00:41] Elena Ruiz: And I'm Elena, solutions engineering. I'll help with the runtime tuning, batching, KV cache notes, and bench tests.
[00:49] [00:50] Ava Thompson: Great. So our immediate constraints: we are in a pretty regulated vertical, so data residency + key management is huge. Also low latency for some features, but cost matters too.
[01:05] Nina Ruiz: to echo that, we need SOC 2 evidence, KMS integration notes, and we have to keep logs for 2 years per compliance.
[01:14] Morgan Lee: Understood. We'll include the SOC material and our security pack in the shared folder. For KMS we support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations are possible but may need enterprise private deployment.
[01:27] Derek Cho: Can you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private again? I know the doc, but for our infra it's about VPC reachability and whether we keep all egress inside our network.
[01:38] Elena Ruiz: Yeah, quick explainer: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in Redwood's managed infra — gives you capacity isolation and predictable throughput, but it's still within Redwood's control plane. Private is where we can deploy a private control plane in your VPC or on-prem, fully customer-networking controlled. Private is usually preferred when you need full VPC-only egress and HSM/KMS that you manage.
[02:05] Ravi Menon: And latency differences?
[02:09] Elena Ruiz: If you run Private on-prem close to your app, you can shave tens of ms. Dedicated is predictable but depends on region proximity. For the pilot we can measure both.
[02:20] [02:21] Ava Thompson: Cool. On the playbook — can we walk through the staging checklist now?
[02:28] Morgan Lee: Absolutely. Slide 1 of the playbook: provisioning. We need a staging VPC CIDR, a peering or private link preference, NAT egress rules, and sample payloads. Derek, you were collecting sample sizes and typical QPS?
[02:43] Derek Cho: Yes, we have two flows: conversational UI with median prompt length ~400 tokens and batch re-rank jobs that run in bursts — maybe 50 requests per second peak for the batch runner, but bursty. For the pilot baseline plan, we'd like to model 5k to 10k tokens per session sample for stress testing.
[03:05] Elena Ruiz: Good — that's helpful. Our bench test plan will mimic that distribution. For batches we recommend separate route with longer time window to allow smart batching.
[03:16] [03:20] Sam (intern): sorry quick question — what is KV cash? I heard that earlier in the docs.
[03:24] Morgan Lee: (laughs) KV cache, yes — key-value cache, sometimes transcribed as cash. It's the model's context cache for streaming conversations, helps reduce repeated token compute for long chats.
[03:33] Ava Thompson: We'll want persistent KV cache for chat continuity. Does that require sticky sessions?
[03:38] Elena Ruiz: Typically we keep the KV cache in the runtime with a session id; for multi-region routing we provide cache replication strategies or fall back to short-term cache with rehydration. We'll document the tradeoffs.
[03:49] [04:00] Nina Ruiz: On the security side — SSO and RBAC: We need SAML with IdP initiated login, SCIM for user provisioning, and granular RBAC so certain teams can't download logs containing PII.
[04:13] Sanjay Patel: We support SAML SSO and SCIM; RBAC is role-based with admin/audit/reader roles. We also have token-level access controls and per-route permissions in the console. We'll include an RBAC matrix in the playbook.
[04:28] Derek Cho: For audit logs, can we push them to our SIEM or do you provide log retention endpoints?
[04:35] Morgan Lee: We can export audit logs to your S3, GCS, or push via SIEM webhook. There's also an option for longer retention with the compliance pack add-on. We'll attach the log exporter docs.
[04:47] [05:00] Ava Thompson: About keys — if we want to use our KMS, is that supported in Dedicated? In Private only?
[05:07] Elena Ruiz: You can integrate customer-managed KMS in both Dedicated and Private, but for full HSM-backed signing you typically see customers go Private. We'll surface the exact encryption-at-rest and in-transit diagrams.
[05:20] Ravi Menon: Ok. Onboarding timeline — what's realistic to get to a pilot run?
[05:25] Sanjay Patel: Typical path is 2-4 weeks for staging + bench tests, then 1 week to iterate, so roughly 3-6 weeks. Since you're regulated and need security review, plan for the upper end unless we fast-track documents.
[05:40] Morgan Lee: We'll target staging provisioning within 5 business days once Derek gives us the CIDR and sample payloads. Then bench tests in the week following.
[05:52] [06:00] Derek Cho: We'll try to have the VPC details and sample payloads by Wed (2027-06-09).
[06:05] Ava Thompson: That works.
[06:07] [06:20] Sam (intern): There's a note in the playbook about prompt specs and guardrails — who owns writing those?
[06:25] Morgan Lee: Typically product and ML collaborate. We can provide prompt templates and safety guardrails; you'll run them through your evals and we can add to the quality monitoring suite in Redwood Optimize.
[06:38] Elena Ruiz: Quick technical note: for the bench we're going to run a 24 hour soak and a 2 hour spike test to simulate bursty traffic. We'll collect p50/p90/p99 latencies and token cost breakdowns.
[06:52] Derek Cho: For token accounting — we need token breakdowns per route and per user. Is that in the console?
[06:59] Sanjay Patel: Yes, console shows token breakdown by route/model and you can attach labels. We'll send a sample dashboard.
[07:08] [07:30] Ava Thompson: One more compliance Q: do you support data residency restrictions at the region level? We need EU-only for some workloads.
[07:38] Morgan Lee: Yes, you can lock model routes to regions; for Private you can run entirely in EU. For Hosted/Dedicated we provision regional capacity — we'll mark the pilot nodes in eu-west for EU traffic.
[07:51] Nina Ruiz: Also we need to see proof of SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs before we spin up staging.
[07:57] Morgan Lee: We'll attach those docs with the playbook.
[08:04] [08:15] Ravi Menon: OK, let's talk ownership of the runbook and what we do if we hit a performance regression during pilot.
[08:22] Elena Ruiz: Good question. Runbook ownership: Redwood provides the activation runbook but we expect your platform eng to co-own the staging environment. If there's a regression, built-in fallback can route to a lower-cost variant or to time-limited fallbacks while we investigate. We also have automated rollback and can pin model versions.
[08:41] Derek Cho: For model rollouts — is canary supported? We want to ramp traffic slowly.
[08:47] Morgan Lee: Yes, we support canary/A-B rollouts via the Console with percentage ramping and automatic rollback conditions.
[08:56] [09:10] Ava Thompson: Does Redwood help with quantization recommendations and quality tradeoffs? We're looking at 4-bit quantized models to save costs.
[09:18] Elena Ruiz: Absolutely. Redwood Optimize recommends quant profiles per workload and we'll run evals on your prompts to validate quality delta. For 4-bit you often see small quality drops that can be mitigated with prompt tuning and short context caching.
[09:33] Sanjay Patel: We'll set up an eval suite against your prompt set as part of the pilot.
[09:39] [10:00] Sam (intern): sorry if this is obvious — what are the typical token cost targets people aim for?
[10:06] Morgan Lee: That varies widely. For chat features, customers set cost buckets per active session; for batch re-rank it's per-response. We'll share example unit economics spreadsheets.
[10:17] Ravi Menon: Sounds good.
[10:20] [10:30] Nina Ruiz: Back to security — will logs include raw user text, and can we redact PII before it's stored?
[10:36] Elena Ruiz: You can configure redaction pipelines; we also support post-processing hooks to strip PII prior to long-term storage. For audit logs we keep metadata and can provide redacted transcripts upon request.
[10:51] [11:05] Derek Cho: Network egress — any special firewall rules on the Redwood side we should account for?
[11:11] Morgan Lee: We'll provide a minimal outbound port list and IP ranges for the nodes. For Private, you control egress fully. For Dedicated we'll need peering or private link; no public internet egress for traffic in that setup unless configured.
[11:26] [11:45] Ava Thompson: Ok, let's lock the pilot success criteria: p95 latency below 500ms for the chat route, throughput handling 50 rps sustained for batch route with 99% success, and cost target below X per 1k tokens — we'll fill X after we see the initial bench.
[11:59] Sanjay Patel: We'll record those as tentative SLOs and refine after the first bench test.
[12:07] [12:20] Morgan Lee: Next — runbook steps: 1) share VPC + creds for peering, 2) Redwood provisions staging nodes, 3) bench tests + monitoring enabled, 4) iterate on quantization/ batching, 5) pilot signoff.
[12:35] Derek Cho: Who will have admin access to the staging console?
[12:39] Sanjay Patel: We'll provision an admin group for your infra team and a read-only group for product/PMs. SCIM will auto-provision in the main tenant.
[12:52] [13:10] Sam (intern): Quick note — there's a mention of "function calling" in the docs; is that the same as external tool calls?
[13:17] Elena Ruiz: Yes, function/tool calling allows the model to emit structured outputs that can trigger downstream functions. We'll include best practices for retries, idempotency, and security for webhooks in the runbook.
[13:29] [13:45] Ava Thompson: Perfect. For the resources you mentioned — where will the playbook and security pack live?
[13:51] Morgan Lee: We'll put everything in a shared Confluence/Drive folder and send a link in the follow-up email. I'll attach the SOC 2, IAM docs, runbooks, and the bench test template.
[14:02] [14:20] Derek Cho: One small nit — our infra folks prefer config-as-code. Can you provide Terraform snippets for the peering and any infra pieces?
[14:30] Elena Ruiz: We do have Terraform examples for peering, S3 export, and VPC endpoints. We'll include those in the repo.
[14:38] [14:50] Ravi Menon: Any blockers we should be aware of?
[14:53] Morgan Lee: The main blocker is getting the VPC details and the compliance checklist signed off. Once we have those, the rest is mostly execution.
[15:02] [15:20] Nina Ruiz: I'll review the compliance pack and get back with questions. Expect an initial list by Thursday (2027-06-10).
[15:29] Ava Thompson: Are there any specific data transforms you'd recommend before sending sample payloads? We have PII in our test set.
[15:36] Elena Ruiz: If possible, sanitize or pseudonymize PII. We'll accept masked tokens; we just need realistic token length and structure. We can also run a small schema check to confirm.
[15:49] [16:05] Morgan Lee: Ok wrapping up — to recap: Morgan will share the activation playbook and the compliance pack by Monday (2027-06-07). Derek will share VPC CIDR and payloads by 2027-06-09. Nina will confirm KMS/compliance questions by 2027-06-10. Elena will produce the bench test plan by 2027-06-11. We'll schedule the bench run for the week of 2027-06-14.
[16:30] Sanjay Patel: I'll create the onboarding sprint in our project tracker and invite all owners.
[16:36] Ava Thompson: Thanks all — this was useful.
[16:40] Morgan Lee: Thanks everyone, talk soon.
[16:45] [END]

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional mis-transcriptions present (KV cash, function calling partial), typical of automated meeting exports.
